opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll is within the allowed maximum (write for full-time employees), so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is above the allowed maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: Note 1 (HR) says Douglas Salinas (E045) is full_time and recommends write, while Note 2 (Security) says he is a contractor with basic security training and recommends read. Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read, and write is above that maximum. Given the conflicting employment-type records, I grant the more restrictive permissible level (read) to stay within policy and avoid overgranting. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and E045's role is Engineer, so admin does not apply in any case.
